extracted.intended_audience: anatomists, physicians, and natural philosophers (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed anatomical and behavioral description of parasitic roundworms (lumbricus species) based on dissection, microscopic examination, and direct observation; includes comparison with prior authorities and implications for diagnosis and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: External morphological description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe outward form and dimensions: "usually about a foot long... about the size of a wheat straw, or a goose quill; their colour white; at both extremes they grow narrow;" mouth composed of "three lips"; anus "a transverse slit a little before the extreme point of the tail."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record size, colour, tapering at ends, presence/absence of feet or asperities on annuli; compare to known taxa (earth-worms, leeches). Give specifics rather than generic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal anatomy and genitalia (male and female)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail internal organs: male with "a penis, a vesicula seminalis, and a testis"; female with "a pudendum, vagina uteri, cornua uteri, and spermatic vessels"; note placement (e.g., penis at tail), structure (convoluted testis), and contents (milky juice in vesicula seminalis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace ducts from orifices to termini; excise and spread genital parts for measurement; compare with earthworms and other animals; record positions and relationships within body cavity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic examination of small structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the microscope to examine head, hooks, papillae, and eggs: observed "a double order of spikes or hooks" in the head; eggs appeared under microscope as "an infinite number of small eggs" and when fresh were "covered with abundance of small asperities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide magnified figures; describe spike arrangement and papillae; examine eggs' surface texture and document changes on drying; include microscope-aided drawings and labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dissection and live observation to determine vitality and individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the organism is a living animal (not merely a membrane) by observing movement and life in severed joints: pieces "voided alive" or kept alive "for ½ of an hour, or more in warm water"; joints contract and change shape, indicating autonomous life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe specimens alive in water and after separation; record duration and quality of motions; note whether separated joints maintain motion and turgidity as evidence against the "many worms in a membrane" hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphological evidence for mouths in each joint
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify protuberances and orifices on edges as mouths: "The protuberances about the middle of the edges of the joints, are the orifices I take for mouths." Note hooks at head and differences in joint extremities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document location and frequency of protuberances; use microscope to show orifice openings; argue why they are mouths (functionally and by observation) rather than other structures (e.g., lungs, vents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refutation of alternative explanations by comparison and logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly confront prior authorities who called the worm a turned intestinal coat, mucus membrane, or many worms included in a membrane (Hippocrates, Aetius, Paulus Aegineta, Mercurialis, Valleriola, Platerus), and show how direct observations (no membrane found, hooks, mouths, regular joint differences) contradict those views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior claims and give empirical counter-evidence from dissections and microscopy; point out logical inconsistencies (e.g., how a membrane would produce hooks or regularly differing joint extremes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen provenance and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Record source and keep specimens: examples include a specimen "voided by a young man in London, 8 yards long, which I still keep by me," and worms taken from a dissected dog; indicate where and how specimens were obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State exact provenance (voided vs dissected, patient age), keep and preserve exemplars for future study, and reference preserved specimens in the report and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative recording and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide measurements and counts: specimen lengths (8 yards, ~5 feet), joint lengths (~4 of an inch), genital vessel lengths ("from each cornu... about four feet"), estimated egg counts ("more than 1000 eggs in each female worm").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report lengths, counts, and proportions where possible; give units and methods; use measurements to support species distinctions and reproductive capacity claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral and locomotory description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe modes of movement: joints contract producing cylinder/round or concave/convex shapes, "bellying out at the edges," multiple simultaneous contractions promoting progression, and lateral protuberances acting "like so many scales... perform the use of feet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and document dynamic shape changes and their sequences; interpret anatomical structures (protuberances, scales) as locomotory adaptations and compare with other worms' locomotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of secretions and mucous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for mucus observed in stools as either intestinal mucus or slime secreted by worms: mucus may be "but the mucus of the intestines themselves, or a slimy spolium cast off from these worms"; leeches and earthworms cast slime when placed in water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform simple comparative tests (place related animals in water) to see mucus production; caution against misidentifying mucus as beds of worms or separate organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical and treatment implications based on identification
rubrics_metrics.description: State that identification affects treatment: "the cure must accordingly be adapted" and give cautions such as Henr. ab Heers's advice to "avoid the giving the powder of these worms for expelling others; since we cannot be secure, but that at the same time we may sow the seed for propagating more."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link diagnostics to therapeutic choices; warn about iatrogenic propagation (e.g., using crushed worms that contain eggs) and recommend treatments appropriate to oviparous vs viviparous interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine reproductive mode with direct evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess claims of viviparity vs oviparity using dissection and microscopy: author argues they are "not viviparous but oviparous," based on cornua uteri "turgid with a milky juice" that under microscope is "nothing else but an infinite number of small eggs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open reproductive organs, inspect contents microscopically, quantify eggs, and use these observations to refute anecdotal viviparity reports arising from misidentification of genital material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of analogies and mechanical models to explain function
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ mechanical analogies to explain motion and structure: e.g., compare spiral muscle and motion to a wire wound on a cylinder which when slipped off brings one end nearer; compare leech teeth arranged in triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate mechanical analogies to clarify observed function, but tie analogies back to empirical observation and avoid overextension of metaphor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration and labeling of figures to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed plates and figure explanations: multiple figures (Pl. 19 figs. 1–13) showing whole worms, head details, protuberances, genital parts, and eggs; label structures (a, b, ccc, d, ee, f, etc.) and give magnifications where used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both macroscopic and microscopic illustrations, give legends explaining each figure and pointed labels corresponding to text descriptions to let readers verify morphological claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of simple experiments and observation under varying conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply basic experimental manipulations: keep severed pieces in warm water to observe motion; cut bodies to see ichor discharge from pores; use vesicatories/blisters and observe clinical effects in case reports; test effects of medicines (e.g., crude mercury, tansy seed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report experimental conditions (temperature, medium), sequence of manipulations, observed responses, and link experimental outcomes to interpretations (life, secretion, therapeutic efficacy).
